purpose: A verifiable method for turning a real household and a dated water-quality result into a correctly sized, locally compliant, leak-controlled water-treatment installation: converting chemistry and demand into per-stage sizing mechanisms, closing a flow and pressure budget, sequencing and placing the train so bypass, drain, air-gap, cross-connection, thermal-expansion and bonding obligations are verified with the authority having jurisdiction rather than assumed, choosing in-house versus subcontracted licensed labor as a cost and accountability mechanism, executing joints and leak controls that keep water damage improbable, and commissioning, orienting and documenting the job so performance is proven against the pre-install reading without a single health claim.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the reader operates a residential water-treatment business that sells, installs and later services the equipment; the reader is not a code official, a laboratory, or a licensed authority on any jurisdiction's rules

water-quality inputs arrive from the diagnostic stage as real, dated test results or the utility's published water-quality report; nothing in this knowledge base is sized from an assumed regional value or from an in-home demonstration

plumbing, permit, discharge, electrical and contractor-licensing requirements differ by jurisdiction and change over time, so each is handled as an obligation class to verify with the authority having jurisdiction on the specific job
no price, margin, labor rate, capacity, flow figure or media-life figure is asserted as fact; every quantity is described as a mechanism whose inputs each individual job supplies
every installation is a permanent alteration of someone's home and water damage is the defining downside risk of the trade
exclusions: segmenting customers by water problem class, running the in-home diagnostic conversation, escalating to an accredited lab as a sales path, and designing the softener, carbon and reverse-osmosis offer architecture: the water-treatment offers and honest diagnostics knowledge base owns all of that, and this one consumes its verified output

replacement schedules per treatment class, service-plan tiers versus a-la-carte pricing, reminder and scheduling systems, retest cadence used as proof of value, churn drivers and referral loops: the filter service plans and retention knowledge base owns all of that, and this one only makes the equipment physically serviceable and hands over the record
any health, medical or disease claim about water, contaminants or treatment; performance statements here are limited to measured changes in the parameters the system was sold to change

asserting any jurisdiction's specific code section, permit fee, inspection rule, discharge limit, protection-device class or contractor-licensing threshold as fact; those are obligation classes to verify locally on every job

invented figures for equipment cost, install labor, subcontract price, gross margin, vessel capacity or media life; those are mechanisms whose inputs come from the job and from the business's own booked history
work outside the water-treatment envelope: well drilling and pump replacement, whole-house repiping, water-heater replacement, septic design, and electrical work beyond the installer's licensed scope
legal, insurance, financial or tax advice, and personalized medical guidance of any kind

in-home demonstration theater such as soap tests, precipitation tricks or electrolysis devices presented as contamination proof, which is never a sizing input and never a substitute for a dated test result

competency_questions.question: What must the pre-install survey capture in this house before anything is quoted, and what findings make a same-day install impossible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRE_INSTALL_SITE_SURVEY lists the tie-in, pipe material and size, pressure observation, drain, power, clearance and access checks and produces a feasibility verdict the quote is built from

competency_questions.question: How do a dated water test and this household's actual usage become the input numbers that size hardware?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WATER_CHEMISTRY_LOAD converts verified results into load parameters and names missing ones, and HOUSEHOLD_DEMAND_PROFILE separates daily volume from peak simultaneous flow

competency_questions.question: How do I size a softener so it neither runs out of capacity in the evening nor wastes salt and regeneration water?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOFTENER_CAPACITY_SIZING gives the grain-load mechanism, the iron compensation, the salt-dose efficiency trade, the reserve, and the service-flow check

competency_questions.question: How do I size carbon and other media so they still work at the household's peak flow, and how much pressure will the finished train actually consume?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARBON_CONTACT_SIZING sizes on contact time at peak flow and on the disinfectant class, and FLOW_AND_PRESSURE_BUDGET closes a measured baseline against per-stage losses with fouling headroom

competency_questions.question: When does a point-of-use reverse-osmosis unit belong in the design, and what does its installation demand that a whole-house system does not?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POU_RO_SIZING explains stored draw-down versus rated production, feed-pressure effects, the concentrate drain and air gap, the faucet penetration approval and under-sink service clearance

competency_questions.question: What changes in the design when the house is on a private well instead of a municipal main?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WELL_VS_MUNICIPAL_ADAPTATION states the pressure-source difference, placement relative to pressure tank and controls, the backwash draw check against the pump, oxidation-before-filtration sequencing, and the boundary with the well contractor

competency_questions.question: In what order should the stages sit, and where does prefiltration go so the expensive media is protected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRETREAT_AND_TRAIN_SEQUENCING gives the protective ordering logic, micron staging, oxidation before filtration, and checks the added stages against the pressure budget

competency_questions.question: Where does the equipment physically go, how is it isolated, and will a technician be able to service it in two years?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POE_PLACEMENT_AND_LOOP fixes the tie-in relative to shutoff, heater and exterior takeoffs, BYPASS_AND_ISOLATION_DESIGN provides bypass, isolation and drain-down, and SERVICE_ACCESS_CLEARANCE guarantees removal clearance and labeling

competency_questions.question: How is the waste side connected so regeneration, backwash and concentrate can never be drawn back into the drinking water, and where is that discharge allowed to go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRAIN_AIRGAP_AND_DISCHARGE requires an air gap or approved receptor, checks the receptor against peak discharge rate and the manufacturer's run limits, and treats the discharge destination as a locally verified obligation class

competency_questions.question: Which plumbing, cross-connection, expansion and electrical obligations does this job class trigger, and how do I answer that without asserting rules I have not verified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CODE_PERMIT_OBLIGATIONS enumerates the obligation classes and the verify-with-the-authority procedure, BACKFLOW_AND_THERMAL_EXPANSION handles cross-connection and closed-system consequences, and ELECTRICAL_AND_BONDING_CONTINUITY handles power and metallic-pipe bonding

competency_questions.question: Should this install be done by my own crew or by a subcontracted licensed plumber, and what does that choice cost me beyond the invoice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSING_AND_LABOR_MODEL treats licensing as a locally verified obligation class and compares fully loaded in-house cost against subcontract price plus coordination and quality variance, naming who owns the customer relationship and the workmanship warranty

competency_questions.question: How do I keep leak and water-damage risk, the catastrophic failure of this trade, inside acceptable bounds?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONNECTION_MATERIALS_AND_JOINTS matches transitions to found materials with torque and dielectric discipline, and LEAK_RISK_CONTROL layers pressure hold, a full dynamic cycle, damage-aware siting, an offered shutoff control and a photographic record

competency_questions.question: What has to be tested, programmed and proven before the crew leaves, and how is that proof stated without making a health claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSIONING_AND_VERIFICATION requires purge and sanitize, programming from verified inputs, an observed full cycle, a flow and pressure check, and a matched pre and post reading limited to the parameters the system was sold to change

competency_questions.question: What does the homeowner receive and understand at handoff, what happens when the job turns out bigger than quoted, and what record survives for warranty and future service?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOMEOWNER_ORIENTATION_HANDOFF demonstrates the bypass and states what the system does not do, SCOPE_INTEGRITY_AND_CHANGE_ORDERS requires stop-document-explain-approve in writing, and INSTALL_RECORD_AND_WARRANTY closes the as-built with settings, serials, photographs, verifications and the warranty boundary

glossary.definition: Treatment installed on the main service line where water enters the house, so every fixture downstream receives treated water; the placement decision that governs whether hot and cold, irrigation and exterior taps are included or split out.
Treatment installed at a single fixture, typically an under-sink reverse-osmosis unit with its own faucet, sized to what one household draws at that tap rather than to whole-house flow.

The hardness the house presents to a softener per day, formed by multiplying the measured hardness concentration by the household's daily volume and adding a compensation where soluble iron also consumes exchange capacity; it is the mechanism that sets regeneration frequency, not a fixed catalog number.

The flow a vessel or housing must pass while treating, which must cover the household's peak simultaneous demand rather than its average draw; the number that frequently decides vessel and valve size before capacity does.

How long water stays inside a media bed at a given flow, determined by bed volume and flow rate together; the mechanism that decides whether adsorptive or catalytic media actually performs at peak demand rather than only at a trickle.

The cycles in which a softener draws brine to restore exchange capacity and a media filter lifts and rinses its bed to the drain; both consume water, demand a drain that can take their peak rate, and are the reason a treatment install is also a waste-side install.

The valve arrangement, integral to the equipment or built as a three-valve loop, that routes water around the treatment train so the house keeps water while the equipment is isolated; also the homeowner's first emergency control during a leak.

A physical, unobstructed vertical separation between the equipment's waste discharge and the receptor's flood level, so waste can never be siphoned back into the potable system; the default acceptable waste connection, with the specific arrangement and any alternative to be verified with the authority having jurisdiction.

The condition created when a check valve, backflow device or meter arrangement stops water flowing back toward the main; heated water then has nowhere to expand, so pressure rises on every water-heater cycle and stresses relief valves, joints and newly installed equipment, with a correctly sized and charged expansion device as the remedy class.

Where a metallic incoming water pipe forms part of the building's electrical grounding or bonding arrangement, cutting it to insert equipment or a plastic bypass can interrupt that path; a jumper across the interruption is the common restoration, and whether it is required and who may install it is an obligation class to verify locally.

nodes.definition: The physical walk of the house before any equipment is promised. The surveyor finds the main service entry and the main shutoff, identifies the pipe material and diameter at the intended tie-in, reads static pressure at a hose bib and watches what happens to it under a running load, locates the water heater and establishes whether the only usable tie-in falls upstream or downstream of it, maps the irrigation and exterior hose takeoffs the customer will not want treated, finds a drain that could take a regeneration or backwash discharge and a receptacle that is not on a switched circuit, measures the working space and the path a tank has to travel to reach it, and records freeze exposure, floor finish, what is stored in the way, and every condition that will otherwise surprise the crew: brittle galvanized runs, prior unpermitted work, a water heater near end of life, a slab layout with no accessible loop. The output is a feasibility verdict plus a survey record that every later sizing, placement, compliance and pricing decision cites by name.

included: main shutoff and tie-in identification
pipe material and diameter at the tie-in
static and flowing pressure observation
drain and receptacle availability
working space, carry path and freeze exposure
condition of existing plumbing and equipment
irrigation and exterior takeoff mapping
a written feasibility verdict
excluded: interpreting the water test or choosing the treatment class
the in-home diagnostic conversation
designing the recurring service plan

pros.claim: A survey converts an unknown house into a quotable, installable job and removes most install-day surprises
pros.example: finding that the only accessible tie-in sits downstream of the water heater, which changes both the placement and the quote before a crew is ever dispatched

cons.claim: Surveying costs a separate trip and slows a same-visit close that a competitor will happily take
cons.example: a rival quoting from a photograph of the garage wall while the survey visit is still being scheduled

failure_modes: quoting from a phone description and discovering on install day that no acceptable drain is within reach
missing a pressure problem so the sized train starves the upstairs fixtures
ignoring the carry path so the vessel does not fit through the crawlspace hatch or basement stair
acceptance_tests: the survey record names the tie-in location, pipe material and diameter, observed static and flowing pressure, drain type and distance, receptacle availability and circuit type, working clearance and carry path, and a signed feasibility verdict issued before the quote
revisit_triggers: the homeowner requests a different equipment location
a remodel, repipe or water-heater replacement occurs between survey and install
the crew reports a condition the survey sheet does not ask about

base.update_signal: a run of installs where the crew repeatedly meets conditions the survey sheet never asked about

nodes.definition: Convert the verified water-quality results handed over by the diagnostic stage into the load parameters that actually determine hardware. Hardness becomes a daily grain load only once it is multiplied by household volume; soluble iron and manganese matter because they consume exchange capacity and because their oxidation state decides whether a softener alone is defensible at all; free chlorine and chloramine are separated because they demand different carbon behaviour and consume media at different rates; pH and alkalinity constrain which oxidation and corrosion choices are available; turbidity, sediment and dissolved solids drive prefiltration and membrane recovery. The node also names what the offered classes do not treat, so nothing silently enters the design as a promise. The governing rule is that a load parameter may come only from a dated test the customer was shown or from the utility's published water-quality report, and where a parameter the design depends on is stale, uncertain, or below the usable range of the method that produced it, an accredited-lab result is obtained before hardware is specified. Nothing here states or implies a health effect; the parameters are engineering inputs.

included: translating verified test values into engineering load parameters
distinguishing disinfectant classes for media selection
iron and manganese oxidation state as a design input
naming parameters that must be retested before sizing
flagging findings the offered classes do not treat
excluded: running the diagnostic conversation or the offer selection
any statement about health effects of a parameter
sizing from an in-home demonstration or a regional assumption

pros.claim: Sizing from this house's dated reading instead of a regional habit keeps the system from being built for water it does not have
pros.example: a well whose measured iron changes the design from a plain softener into oxidation plus filtration ahead of it

cons.claim: Insisting on an accredited-lab result for the uncertain parameter costs calendar time and sometimes the job
cons.example: waiting on a laboratory turnaround for a specific-contaminant question while the customer keeps taking quotes

failure_modes: sizing from a field kit reading that a laboratory would not support
treating a municipal system average as this address's value
carrying a free-chlorine assumption into a chloraminated supply and specifying the wrong media class
acceptance_tests: every load parameter used in sizing traces to a dated test record or the utility's published report, and any parameter the design depends on without a defensible reading is listed as an open item before hardware is ordered
revisit_triggers: a retest or a new utility report shows the source chemistry has moved
the utility changes its disinfection practice
the well is serviced or deepened, or the house is switched between well and municipal supply

base.update_signal: a laboratory retest contradicts the field reading the design was sized from

nodes.definition: Build the demand side of sizing, which is two different numbers that size two different things. How many people live in the house and how they use water produces a daily volume that drives capacity, consumable load and regeneration frequency; the fixture inventory and the realistic pattern of simultaneous use produce a peak flow that the vessel, valve and every housing must pass without starving the house. A soaking tub, a multi-head shower, a high-draw appliance or an irrigation zone hanging off the same line changes the peak far more than it changes the daily total. Occupancy given at the kitchen table is a starting estimate to be reconciled against the meter or the utility's billing history wherever that is available, and the profile carries an explicit note of announced changes, because a system sized to a two-person household will be regenerating early once the finished suite is occupied.

included: occupancy and usage-pattern intake
fixture and simultaneous-use inventory
daily volume estimate reconciled against billing or meter data
peak simultaneous flow requirement
announced future changes in occupancy or fixtures
excluded: choosing the treatment class
the consumable replacement cadence sold to the customer
irrigation system design

pros.claim: Separating peak flow from daily volume prevents the classic error of sizing an entire system on one number
pros.example: a modest-use household whose two-head shower would drop pressure through the compact housing the daily figure alone would have justified

cons.claim: Self-reported usage is soft data and households change faster than equipment does
cons.example: an occupancy figure given at the table that omits two adult children about to move back in

failure_modes: sizing on occupancy alone while irrigation is drawn through the treated line
adopting a peak flow from a specification sheet instead of the flow this house will actually create
ignoring a stated upcoming occupancy change and sizing for today
acceptance_tests: the profile states a daily volume basis, a peak simultaneous flow basis, the source of each as stated, metered or billing-derived, and any announced upcoming change
revisit_triggers: occupancy or usage pattern changes materially
irrigation or a high-draw appliance is added to the treated line
the customer reports pressure loss or early capacity exhaustion after install

base.update_signal: billing or meter data contradicts the household's self-reported usage

nodes.definition: Hold the map of obligation classes a water-treatment installation can trigger, without asserting any jurisdiction's specifics. The classes are: whether the work requires a permit and an inspection and who is entitled to pull it; which adopted plumbing code and which local amendments govern the connection and the materials; cross-connection and backflow rules that reach the drain, the brine tank and any hose used for filling or sanitizing; discharge rules for regeneration and backwash waste, where sewer authorities, septic authorities and water-scarce jurisdictions each impose their own limits and some restrict certain equipment classes outright; electrical requirements wherever the equipment plugs in; and product-listing expectations for anything touching potable water. The operating rule is that each of these is verified with the authority having jurisdiction and the currently adopted code before the job is sold, never recited from memory or transplanted from a neighbouring county, and that the verification is written into the job record with the source, the person or document consulted, and the date.

included: enumerating the obligation classes a treatment install can trigger
the verify-with-the-authority-having-jurisdiction procedure
recording what was verified, with whom and when
escalating to a licensed professional when the answer is ambiguous
excluded: stating any code section, permit fee, inspection rule or licensing threshold as universally true
legal advice
obligations outside the water-treatment install envelope

pros.claim: Working from obligation classes plus local verification lets the business enter a new county without re-teaching the crew a memorized rulebook
pros.example: verification revealing that a neighbouring authority treats regeneration discharge to a septic system differently from the home county

cons.claim: Verification consumes calendar time and sometimes returns the answer that ends the sale
cons.example: learning after the customer has chosen a system that the equipment class is restricted for that service area

failure_modes: assuming the last jurisdiction's rules travel with the truck
skipping a permit that surfaces later at resale or during an unrelated inspection
quoting a code specific in a sales conversation that turns out to be wrong
acceptance_tests: the job record names each obligation class checked, the authority or document consulted, the date and the disposition, and no code, permit or licensing specific appears in customer-facing material without a dated local verification behind it
revisit_triggers: the business begins selling in a new jurisdiction
a code cycle is adopted or locally amended
an inspector or authority corrects an assumption the business had been operating on

base.update_signal: an authority having jurisdiction states a requirement that differs from what the job record assumed

nodes.definition: Decide who is permitted to make the connection and who actually makes it. The licensing question is an obligation class: some jurisdictions and some scopes of work require a licensed plumbing or specialty contractor, some treat an equipment set on existing stubs as a lesser scope, and the answer must be verified locally rather than inferred from how a neighbouring state operates. The labor question is economic and reputational. An in-house installer gives scheduling control, one enforceable quality standard, direct accountability for the leak record and a falling marginal cost per job once the calendar fills, but carries payroll, vehicle, tooling, insurance and training cost that must be covered in slow weeks too. A subcontracted licensed plumber converts that fixed cost into a per-job variable cost, often carries their own license and insurance, and absorbs some exposure, but competes with their own customers for your schedule, varies in workmanship, and stands in the doorway of the relationship the recurring service revenue depends on. The comparison is a mechanism, not a figure: fully loaded hourly cost multiplied by realistic job hours plus your own callback and rework rate on one side, against quoted subcontract price plus coordination overhead plus the cost of quality variance on the other, both computed from the business's own booked jobs.

included: contractor-licensing obligation class and its local verification
fully loaded in-house cost versus subcontract price as a comparison mechanism
insurance and workmanship-warranty allocation
who owns the customer relationship at the door
written subcontract terms covering scope discipline and customer ownership
excluded: any stated wage, subcontract price or margin figure
recurring service-plan economics
employment or legal advice

pros.claim: Framing labor as a fixed-versus-variable cost decision ties the choice to booked volume rather than to preference
pros.example: a business with an uneven winter calendar staying on subcontract labor until install weeks are consistently full

cons.claim: Subcontracting hands the customer moment, and part of the service annuity, to a third party
cons.example: a plumber who does clean work but tells the homeowner to call him directly for future filter changes

failure_modes: assuming a license class or exemption transfers across jurisdictions
using unlicensed labor for work that required a licensed contractor
comparing a subcontract quote against a bare wage instead of a fully loaded cost
acceptance_tests: the labor decision cites the verified local licensing requirement for this work scope, a fully loaded in-house cost basis built from the business's own jobs, and a named owner of the customer relationship and of the workmanship warranty
revisit_triggers: install volume moves materially up or down
a subcontractor's callback or complaint rate rises
licensing requirements change or the business expands into a new jurisdiction

base.update_signal: the business's own booked-job costing shows the loaded in-house cost crossing the subcontract price

nodes.definition: Govern what happens between the quote and the wrench. The quoted scope is built from what the survey actually found, and when open pipe reveals work the survey could not see, the crew stops, photographs the condition, explains in plain language what it is, what correcting it costs and what happens if it is deferred, and obtains a recorded approval before continuing. It is never a verbal upsell delivered to someone standing over a cut pipe with the water off. The same discipline forbids using the moment of maximum leverage to enlarge the system beyond what the chemistry and the demand profile justify, forbids any framing that suggests the household's water is endangering their health, and demands extra care where the customer is elderly, alone, unwell or visibly not following: offer to pause, to include a family member or trusted contact, or to reschedule rather than closing on the spot. Where a customer declines an item, the crew leaves the house with water restored and the declined item written down, not with pressure applied.

included: quoting only from survey findings
the stop, document, explain and approve sequence for discovered conditions
written change-order approval before work resumes
vulnerable-customer pacing rules
the prohibition on fear framing and on install-moment upsizing
excluded: the in-home diagnostic and offer conversation
pricing strategy or any stated price
the service-plan sale at handoff

pros.claim: A documented stop-and-approve rule protects the customer and the crew from a dispute neither can reconstruct later
pros.example: a photographed corroded shutoff with a written approval, and no argument at invoicing about who authorized the extra work

cons.claim: Pausing for approval costs crew hours and occasionally loses an add-on that a verbal pitch would have closed
cons.example: a half-day job stretching while the homeowner reaches a spouse to approve replacing a failing shutoff

failure_modes: presenting a discovered condition as an emergency to force a same-hour decision
enlarging the equipment at install time on a story the test data does not support
leaving the water off as unspoken pressure while a price is negotiated
acceptance_tests: every scope change carries a dated photograph of the condition, a written explanation including the option to defer, and the customer's recorded approval logged before the work proceeded
revisit_triggers: a complaint, review or chargeback names install-day charges or pressure
the same discovered condition recurs across jobs and should have been a survey item
a crew member or subcontractor is reported for pressuring a customer

base.update_signal: a customer complaint or public review names install-day pressure or an unexplained charge

nodes.definition: Size an ion-exchange softener from the mechanism rather than from a catalog tier. The daily grain load is the measured hardness multiplied by the household's daily volume, with a compensation added where soluble iron is present because it consumes exchange capacity alongside hardness. Resin volume and the salt dose per regeneration together set the capacity available between regenerations, and the same resin yields more capacity per regeneration at a heavy salt dose and more capacity per unit of salt at a light one: that trade is what the customer pays for every month in salt and in regeneration water, so it is presented as a choice with consequences rather than a factory setting. A reserve must cover what the household will draw between the moment the meter reaches its trigger and the programmed regeneration window, otherwise hard water arrives at the evening shower. Finally the vessel and control valve must pass the peak simultaneous flow from the demand profile within the pressure the budget allows, and on many houses that flow requirement, not capacity, is what actually decides the vessel. Oversizing wastes salt and water per unit of hardness removed and lets resin sit unused between long intervals; undersizing produces the complaint that the softener stopped working.

included: grain-load computation as a mechanism
iron compensation on exchange capacity
resin volume and salt-dose efficiency trade
reserve capacity and regeneration timing
service-flow and pressure-drop check
consequences of over and under sizing
excluded: salt and consumable replenishment scheduling and its pricing
the decision to sell a softener at all
any capacity figure presented as a universal rule

pros.claim: Sizing from grain load and flow makes the regeneration interval and the monthly salt consumption predictable and explainable to the customer
pros.example: showing a household why the higher salt setting buys capacity between regenerations but raises what they carry in from the store

cons.claim: The efficiency trade has no single correct answer and depends on what this customer values
cons.example: a household on a metered sewer that cares more about regeneration water than about salt cost

failure_modes: sizing on hardness alone while measured iron quietly consumes capacity
choosing a vessel that satisfies capacity but chokes the peak flow
programming the valve's hardness value from a guess rather than from the verified test
acceptance_tests: the sizing sheet shows the grain-load basis with its inputs, the iron compensation where applicable, the reserve assumption, the expected regeneration interval and a service-flow check against the profile's peak flow
revisit_triggers: a retest shows hardness or iron has moved
the customer reports hard water late in the day or a jump in salt use
occupancy or irrigation load changes

base.update_signal: observed regeneration intervals across installed accounts diverge from what the grain-load basis predicted

nodes.definition: Size carbon and other adsorptive or catalytic media on contact, never on housing size. The bed must hold water long enough at this household's service flow for the intended reduction to occur, so bed volume and peak flow together determine the contact time, and a bed that performs at an average draw can be short-circuited the moment two fixtures run. Media class follows the disinfectant the utility actually uses, because chloramine behaves differently from free chlorine and generally asks for a catalytic media class or a longer bed. Media life is a load mechanism rather than a calendar fact: the total volume treated multiplied by the concentration being reduced consumes the bed, which is why an identical tank exhausts at different times in two houses on the same street. Backwashing configurations add a further constraint, because the bed must be lifted at a backwash flow the supply can deliver and discharged to a drain that can take it; where either fails, the honest answer is an upflow or cartridge configuration instead, with its own consumable behaviour.

included: contact-time sizing evaluated at peak flow
media class matched to the disinfectant and the target
media life reasoned as a treated-volume load
backwash flow and drain feasibility
upflow and cartridge alternatives where backwash cannot be supported
excluded: the replacement cadence and price sold to the customer
claims about health effects of any substance reduced
the offer-stage decision to include carbon

pros.claim: Contact-time sizing prevents the common failure where taste and odour return only under heavy use
pros.example: a household whose morning peak pushes flow past what the small bed can hold long enough to act

cons.claim: A bed sized for contact at peak flow is physically larger and costs space and money the customer may resist
cons.example: a garage corner that takes one tank comfortably and a second only if a freezer moves

failure_modes: sizing carbon by housing diameter or by whatever the last job used
ignoring chloramine and promising performance measured on free chlorine
specifying a backwashing tank where the supply or the drain cannot carry the backwash rate
acceptance_tests: the sizing sheet states bed volume, the peak flow used, the resulting contact time, the disinfectant class it was matched to, and a backwash flow and drain check wherever the configuration backwashes
revisit_triggers: the utility changes disinfectant or its dose regime
the customer reports taste or odour returning well before the expected media life
peak demand rises through added fixtures or occupancy

base.update_signal: installed beds exhaust materially earlier or later than the treated-volume load model predicted

nodes.definition: Design the point-of-use side, which is a different install problem from the whole-house train. A reverse-osmosis unit under a sink produces slowly and stores what it makes, so the capacity the family experiences is the tank's usable draw-down at this house's line pressure, not the membrane's rated daily production; low feed pressure both slows production and worsens recovery, which is the problem a permeate pump or booster addresses. The installation carries its own requirement set: a concentrate drain connection with an accepted air-gap arrangement, a dedicated faucet penetration in a counter or sink deck that the homeowner must approve on sight because it cannot be undone, a cold feed with its own shutoff, an optional refrigerator or ice-maker tie-in whose long run is its own leak exposure and needs its own isolation, and clearance under the cabinet to change cartridges and the membrane without emptying the cupboard. Feed conditions decide membrane life, which is why a unit placed downstream of whole-house treatment routinely outlives the same unit installed alone on hard, sediment-bearing water.

included: stored draw-down versus rated production reasoning
feed-pressure effects and boosting options
concentrate drain and air-gap arrangement
counter or deck penetration approved on sight
refrigerator tie-in exposure and isolation
under-sink service clearance
interaction with upstream whole-house treatment
excluded: cartridge replacement scheduling and plan pricing
contaminant-specific health claims
the offer-stage decision to include reverse osmosis

pros.claim: Explaining stored draw-down rather than rated production sets the expectation that decides whether the customer is satisfied
pros.example: a family that fills large bottles discovering the tank empties faster than the unit refills it

cons.claim: The point-of-use install adds permanent penetrations and a second drain connection, each an irreversible alteration and a leak point
cons.example: a drilled stone counter that cannot be undone if the customer later dislikes where the faucet sits

failure_modes: presenting rated production as usable flow at the faucet
drilling a counter without explicit approval of the exact position
running a refrigerator line with no shutoff and no leak protection
acceptance_tests: the design records the measured feed pressure, the storage and draw-down expectation as explained to the customer, the drain and air-gap arrangement, written approval of any counter penetration, and the service clearance under the cabinet
revisit_triggers: the customer reports slow refill or weak flow at the dedicated faucet
house pressure changes or a pressure-reducing device is added
a refrigerator or ice maker is tied into the line after install

base.update_signal: support calls about slow refill cluster on a particular unit class or feed-pressure band

nodes.definition: Adapt the whole design to which supply the house is on, because the two present themselves very differently at the equipment. A municipal house arrives at a fairly stable pressure carrying a disinfectant residual, so design attention goes to the disinfectant class, to sediment shed by the distribution main after a hydrant event or a repair, and to whether a meter check valve or pressure-reducing arrangement has already turned the house into a closed system. A private well arrives from a pump and a pressure tank, so the design must respect the pump's cycling and the pressure band it maintains, keep backwash and regeneration draws from starving the pump or the household, sit correctly relative to the pressure tank and any existing pump controls, and handle the untreated-source realities a utility would otherwise have handled: grit and sediment, iron and manganese that may need oxidation before any filtration can catch them, sulfur odour, and the bacteriological question, which belongs to accredited-lab testing and to the well owner's own program rather than to a sales conversation. Well work also touches equipment the business may not be licensed to modify, so the boundary with the well or pump contractor is drawn in writing before the job starts.

included: pressure-source behaviour differences between well and municipal supply
placement relative to pressure tank and pump controls
backwash and regeneration draw checked against pump capability
oxidation before filtration for iron, manganese and sulfur
the written scope boundary with the well or pump contractor
routing bacteriological questions to accredited testing
excluded: well drilling, pump replacement or any work reserved to a well contractor
any health claim about untreated well water
the diagnostic sale and its testing program

pros.claim: Treating a well as a pressure system rather than as a tap prevents designs that starve or short-cycle the pump
pros.example: a backwashing filter whose draw exceeds what the pump delivers, cycling it every time the bed lifts

cons.claim: Well designs need more stages and cost more, which loses head-to-head comparisons against a simpler municipal-style quote
cons.example: a competitor quoting a single softener for water that needs oxidation ahead of it

failure_modes: dropping a municipal-style train onto a well without checking pump and tank behaviour
specifying a backwash rate the pump cannot sustain
adjusting pump controls without the license or the well contractor present
acceptance_tests: the design states the supply type, the observed pressure-source behaviour, the backwash draw checked against pump and tank, the pretreatment sequence for any oxidizable load, and the written scope boundary with the well contractor
revisit_triggers: the well is serviced or deepened or the pump is replaced
seasonal chemistry shifts appear in retests
the property is connected to a municipal supply

base.update_signal: well installs show pump cycling or pressure complaints that municipal installs of the same design do not

nodes.definition: Keep a running budget of the pressure the house has against the pressure the proposed train will consume, because every vessel, cartridge housing, valve, fitting and elbow takes a share, the losses accumulate along the series, and they grow sharply as flow rises, so a train that measures acceptably at a single open tap can be unacceptable when two showers run. The budget starts from the static pressure observed at the survey and the pressure seen under a running load, subtracts an allowance for each stage taken at the profile's peak flow from the manufacturer's own pressure-drop curve rather than from an assumption, keeps headroom for media and cartridges that will foul between service visits, and compares the remainder against what the fixtures and appliances in this house need. When the budget does not close, the honest options are a larger vessel or valve, fewer stages in series, a different configuration, or a supply-side correction where the incoming pressure itself is weak and the work is inside the business's licensed scope. Installing anyway and hoping the customer does not notice the shower is not one of them.

included: static and flowing pressure baseline
per-stage loss allowance at peak flow from manufacturer curves
fouling headroom between service visits
the closure check against fixture requirements
the remedy options when the budget fails to close
excluded: pressure-regulator or supply-line work outside the treatment envelope or beyond the licensed scope
the service schedule that keeps fouling in check
fixture replacement

pros.claim: A written pressure budget turns the most common post-install complaint into a design decision made before the sale
pros.example: a plan showing that three cartridge stages in series would leave the upstairs shower short at peak

cons.claim: Honest budgeting sometimes forces a larger or simpler system than the customer intended to buy
cons.example: telling a customer that the compact unit they found online cannot pass their peak flow

failure_modes: using a single-tap reading as the design baseline
ignoring how losses accumulate across stages in series
forgetting that fouled media and loaded cartridges take more pressure than new ones
acceptance_tests: the budget shows the measured baseline, the per-stage allowance at peak flow with its source, the fouling headroom, and a closing margin above what the house's fixtures require
revisit_triggers: the customer reports pressure loss at any fixture
a stage is added to an existing train
supply pressure changes at the meter or the well, or service intervals stretch

base.update_signal: post-install pressure complaints appear on jobs whose budget was recorded as closing

nodes.definition: Decide what sits in front of what and why, because the same components in a different order produce a different service life and a different failure. The organising logic is that each stage protects the one behind it: coarse sediment and grit come out before anything with media, a valve seat or a membrane; oxidation precedes the filtration meant to catch what it precipitates; media that is expensive or slow to replace sits behind a cheap consumable that takes the fouling load; and equipment sensitive to a disinfectant sits behind the stage that reduces it. Sequencing is also a service and economics decision, because placing the sacrificial cartridge where the load falls converts what would have been an early media replacement into an inexpensive routine change. Micron staging follows the same reasoning: jumping straight to a fine filter blinds it quickly, while stepping down keeps each stage inside its working range. Every added stage costs pressure and adds a joint, so the sequence is agreed against the pressure budget and the leak-risk standard rather than drawn in isolation.

included: protective ordering logic across stages
oxidation before filtration
micron staging
placing the sacrificial consumable where the load falls
sequence checked against the pressure budget and joint count
excluded: replacement pricing, reminders and plan cadence
the treatment class selection itself
media manufacturing claims

pros.claim: Ordering the train so a cheap stage absorbs the load converts a costly media replacement into an inexpensive cartridge change
pros.example: a sediment prefilter ahead of a carbon tank on a well that sheds grit after every heavy draw

cons.claim: Each protective stage adds a pressure loss, a leak point and one more thing to service
cons.example: a three-stage prefilter bank that solves fouling but adds three unions the technician must check on every visit

failure_modes: putting a fine filter first and blinding it within weeks
placing oxidation downstream of the filter that was meant to catch the precipitate
adding stages until the pressure budget quietly stops closing
acceptance_tests: the layout drawing shows the ordered stages with the protective reason each one precedes the next, and the accumulated loss at peak flow is inside the pressure budget
revisit_triggers: prefilters foul materially faster than the design expected
a stage is added to or removed from an installed train
source chemistry or supply type changes

base.update_signal: service visits show a downstream stage fouling that the upstream stage was placed to protect

nodes.definition: Choose where the equipment physically lands and how the loop is cut into the service line. The placement sits after the main shutoff and, where the house has them, after the meter and any pressure-reducing arrangement; upstream of the water heater so that treated water reaches both hot and cold; downstream of or split from the irrigation and exterior hose supply the customer does not want treated, since softened water on a lawn is money sent down the drain and untreated outside taps are usually what the household expects; within reach of a drain arrangement that can be made acceptable and of a receptacle that is not switched; out of freeze exposure or inside a protected enclosure where the climate demands it; on a surface that can carry the weight of a full vessel; and in a spot where an eventual leak would be seen and drained rather than absorbed by a finished room. The geometry of the loop itself is decided in the same act, because a placement that satisfies every hydraulic and compliance requirement but leaves no room to service the equipment has simply moved the cost into the future.

included: order relative to shutoff, meter, water heater and exterior takeoffs
drain and receptacle reach
freeze exposure and vessel weight
leak-consequence-aware siting
loop geometry decided together with placement
customer agreement to the location
excluded: the detailed waste-side requirements
the bypass hardware specification
relocating gas, structural or electrical elements

pros.claim: Siting equipment where a leak drains rather than soaks converts the worst failure mode into a nuisance
pros.example: a garage slab beside a floor drain instead of the finished basement wall the customer first suggested

cons.claim: The technically best location is often the one the customer least wants to look at or give up
cons.example: a homeowner refusing the garage wall the survey chose because it is where the bicycles hang

failure_modes: tying in downstream of the water heater and treating only the cold side
sending softened water to the irrigation zone because the takeoff was never mapped
placing a vessel where it cannot be freeze-protected, drained or supported
acceptance_tests: the placement drawing shows the tie-in relative to shutoff, meter, water heater and exterior takeoffs, the drain and receptacle distances, freeze protection where applicable, the load-bearing surface, and the customer's recorded agreement to the location
revisit_triggers: the customer requests relocation after install
a remodel or a change of use alters the space
a leak or freeze event occurs at the chosen location

base.update_signal: relocation requests or leak-damage claims cluster on a particular placement pattern

nodes.definition: Build the install so the equipment can be taken out of service without taking the house out of service. That means a working bypass at the equipment, whether an integral valve or a three-valve loop, isolation valves on both sides of the treatment train, unions or an equally serviceable disconnect so a vessel can come out without cutting pipe, and a drain-down provision so a vessel can be emptied where it stands rather than carried full. The bypass is also the homeowner's emergency tool: it is what they operate when the equipment leaks, when the water suddenly tastes wrong, or when a technician talks them through a fault by phone, so it must be reachable without moving stored belongings, labelled in plain words, and demonstrated at handoff rather than hidden behind the tank. Where the design deliberately leaves an appliance or an exterior tap untreated, that split is plumbed into the same loop while the pipe is already open, never promised as a later visit.

included: bypass and isolation hardware
unions or serviceable disconnects
drain-down provision
labelling and physical reachability
designed untreated splits plumbed at install time
excluded: whole-house shutoff or supply-line replacement beyond the treatment envelope
the homeowner training session itself
service-plan design

pros.claim: A reachable, labelled bypass turns a midnight leak into a valve turn instead of an emergency call and a wet floor
pros.example: a homeowner bypassing the system on the phone while the on-call technician is still driving

cons.claim: A full bypass and isolation set adds fittings, cost and additional potential leak points to every install
cons.example: three extra joints that each have to hold through the pressure test before the crew can leave

failure_modes: relying on the whole-house shutoff instead of local isolation, so any service call shuts off the house
installing a bypass the homeowner cannot reach or recognise
hard-plumbing a vessel with no unions so the first service visit requires cutting pipe
acceptance_tests: the installed loop isolates on both sides, the bypass is physically operated and verified during commissioning, it is labelled, and the drain-down path is demonstrated
revisit_triggers: a service visit requires cutting pipe to remove a component
a homeowner on a support call cannot find or operate the bypass
an untreated split that was promised turns out not to have been plumbed

base.update_signal: support calls or service visits reveal bypasses that customers cannot operate

nodes.definition: Get the waste side right, because it is where a water-treatment install most often collides with plumbing rules. Backwashing filters, regenerating softeners and reverse-osmosis concentrate all discharge to a drain, and the connection has to be made so that waste can never be drawn back into the potable system: the accepted arrangement is an air gap or an approved receptor, not a hose pushed down a standpipe and taped in place. The receptor must accept the equipment's peak discharge rate rather than its average, and the run must respect the manufacturer's stated limits on length and vertical rise, because a long or elevated run raises back pressure and can defeat the cycle the customer is paying for. Where the discharge goes is a separate question with its own answer per jurisdiction: sanitary sewer, a septic system, a laundry standpipe, a condensate line and an exterior discharge are not interchangeable, and several of them are restricted, particularly regeneration brine, which some sewer and septic authorities and some water-scarce jurisdictions limit or prohibit. Each of these is verified with the authority having jurisdiction before the equipment is set, and the verification is dated in the job record.

included: air-gap or approved-receptor connection
receptor capacity at peak discharge rate
run length and vertical rise within manufacturer limits
discharge destination as a locally verified obligation class
dating the verification in the job record
excluded: asserting any jurisdiction's specific discharge limit as fact
septic system design or repair
sewer connection work outside the treatment envelope

pros.claim: Making the air gap the default waste connection renders cross-connection failure structurally unlikely rather than merely unlikely in practice
pros.example: an approved receptor at the laundry standpipe instead of a discharge hose zip-tied into the pipe

cons.claim: Air-gap and receptor requirements constrain placement and sometimes push the equipment away from the ideal tie-in
cons.example: moving the train across the garage because the only acceptable receptor is on the far wall

failure_modes: pushing the drain line into a standpipe with no air gap and creating a cross-connection
running the drain uphill beyond what the valve can push, so cycles fail silently
discharging regeneration waste to a destination the local authority restricts
acceptance_tests: the waste connection is an air gap or approved receptor, the run is inside the manufacturer's length and rise limits, the receptor is verified to accept the peak discharge rate, and the discharge destination carries a dated local verification
revisit_triggers: the local authority changes its discharge or cross-connection rules
the receptor backs up, overflows or is remodelled away
the equipment class or its discharge rate changes

base.update_signal: an inspector, sewer authority or septic authority states a discharge requirement the job record did not anticipate

nodes.definition: Handle the two coupled consequences of inserting devices into a service line. The first is cross-connection control: every point where potable water can meet water that is no longer potable, including the regeneration drain, the brine tank, a hose used for filling or sanitizing and a reverse-osmosis concentrate line, is a cross-connection question whose required protection class is set by the local authority rather than by preference or habit. The second is the closed-system effect: where a check valve, a backflow preventer or a meter arrangement stops water flowing back toward the main, water heated in the water heater has nowhere to expand, so pressure rises on every heating cycle and stresses the relief valve, the heater, the joints and the equipment just installed. The remedy class is a correctly sized and correctly charged expansion device, and whether the house already has one is a survey question rather than a discovery to be made after the fact. The rule is that the install must not silently create a closed system: where it may have done so, the condition is identified, disclosed to the customer and corrected inside the scope the business is licensed to perform or referred out in writing.

included: identifying cross-connection points the install creates or touches
the locally verified protection class for each
recognising and disclosing a closed system
expansion device as a remedy class with a correct charge
referral in writing when the remedy is out of scope
excluded: backflow device testing or certification where that is a separately licensed activity
naming any jurisdiction's device class as universal
water-heater replacement

pros.claim: Asking the closed-system question at survey time prevents the callback where the customer blames the new equipment for a discharging relief valve
pros.example: finding an existing check valve at the meter and pricing the expansion remedy into the job instead of arguing about it a month later

cons.claim: Raising the issue can enlarge the job into work the customer did not plan and the crew may not be licensed to perform
cons.example: an unaddressed closed system that needs a plumber before the treatment work can legitimately proceed

failure_modes: installing a check-valve-bearing device into a system with no expansion provision
dismissing an already discharging relief valve as a normal nuisance
treating a cross-connection question as a matter of preference rather than a verified requirement
acceptance_tests: the job record identifies every cross-connection point the install creates or touches with its locally verified protection class, states whether the system is closed, and shows the expansion provision verified or the referral issued in writing
revisit_triggers: a relief valve begins discharging after install
the utility fits a check valve or replaces the meter
local cross-connection or backflow rules change

base.update_signal: relief-valve or expansion complaints appear on installs the survey recorded as open systems

nodes.definition: Cover the two electrical facts of a plumbing install. The equipment needs power: control valves, pumps, ultraviolet systems and leak-shutoff devices need a receptacle within reach of their cord, on a circuit that will not be killed by a wall switch or shared with a load that trips it, protected as the local requirement class demands for that location, since garages, basements, crawlspaces and outdoor enclosures commonly carry additional protection requirements that must be verified locally, and with the cord routed so it cannot lie in the water a leak would create. The second fact is easier to miss: where the incoming metallic water pipe forms part of the building's electrical grounding or bonding arrangement, cutting it to insert equipment, a plastic bypass or a dielectric transition can interrupt that path, and restoring continuity, commonly with a jumper across the interruption, is a requirement class to verify locally and, where it falls outside the installer's licensed scope, to hand to a qualified electrician in writing rather than to leave undone because the panel is already closed.

included: receptacle availability, circuit suitability and locally verified protection class
cord routing away from a leak path
recognising interruption of metallic-pipe bonding
continuity restoration as a verified requirement class
written referral to a qualified electrician
excluded: performing electrical work beyond the installer's licensed scope
asserting a specific electrical requirement as universal
ultraviolet or pump product selection

pros.claim: Making bonding continuity a standing checklist item catches a hazard that becomes invisible the moment the work is buttoned up
pros.example: a metallic service pipe interrupted by a plastic bypass assembly with no jumper fitted across it

cons.claim: The checklist item frequently pulls in a trade the job never budgeted for
cons.example: an electrician visit to restore continuity in a house whose water pipe is part of the grounding arrangement

failure_modes: plugging a control valve into a switched receptacle so regeneration silently stops
leaving a cord or transformer where a leak will reach it
interrupting a bonded metallic pipe and leaving the continuity unrestored
acceptance_tests: the install record shows an unswitched receptacle with its locally verified protection class, cord routing above the leak path, and either bonding continuity confirmed and restored or a written referral to a qualified electrician
revisit_triggers: the customer reports the system lost power or stopped regenerating
a repipe or panel change alters the grounding arrangement
local electrical requirements for the equipment location change

base.update_signal: an inspector or electrician finds an interrupted bonding path on a completed treatment install

nodes.definition: Install for the second visit, not only the first. Every recurring dollar this business earns is collected by a technician who has to reach the equipment, so the layout must leave the swing space a cartridge housing needs to come down, the head clearance to lift a media tank or pull a riser, room to open and fill a brine tank, a carry path wide enough to take a vessel in and out, and enough light to work by. Labelling belongs to the same unit of work: each stage marked with what it is and which consumable it takes, the flow direction visible, the bypass identified, and the install date and configuration recorded on the equipment itself so a different technician two years later is not reverse-engineering the train with a flashlight. A cheap install squeezed into a tight corner quietly taxes every future service call, and enough of that tax turns a service plan unprofitable or pushes the customer toward whoever can actually reach the filters.

included: clearance for cartridge and media service
brine tank access for filling
carry path for vessels
labelling of stages, consumables, flow direction and bypass
an on-equipment record for the next technician
excluded: service-plan design, cadence and pricing
the customer training session
consumable stocking and logistics

pros.claim: Clearance designed in at install time keeps every later filter change short and predictable
pros.example: a housing that unscrews without moving a shelf, so a service call is a short stop rather than an hour of furniture moving

cons.claim: Service clearance competes with the homeowner's use of the space and sometimes with the best hydraulic position
cons.example: a customer who wants the tank tucked behind shelving that would block the media port

failure_modes: fitting equipment into a corner where a housing cannot be unscrewed without draining and disassembly
leaving stages unlabelled so a later technician fits the wrong cartridge
placing a brine tank where it cannot be filled without moving it
acceptance_tests: at commissioning the technician demonstrates removal clearance for every serviceable component, and labelling names each stage, its consumable and the flow direction
revisit_triggers: a service visit runs materially long because of access
the customer stores belongings that block the equipment
a technician fits the wrong consumable because labelling was ambiguous

base.update_signal: service labour hours per visit differ systematically between placement patterns

nodes.definition: Make the joints in a way that survives this house's materials, temperature and pressure. The pipe material found at survey decides the transition: copper, cross-linked polyethylene, chlorinated polyvinyl chloride, galvanized steel and older plastic systems each have their own accepted transition methods and their own hazards, joining dissimilar metals invites galvanic corrosion unless the transition is dielectric, and aged galvanized pipe frequently disintegrates when disturbed and turns a clean tie-in into a repipe conversation that belongs to the scope-integrity rule. Method selection is a genuine trade, since soldering, pressing, push-to-connect, threading and compression each buy speed or serviceability at a different reliability and tooling cost, and each carries its own discipline: support and clean the joint, respect the manufacturer's sealant and torque instructions on plastic bypass and valve threads which are routinely destroyed by pipe dope or by an installer's idea of tight, use materials listed for potable water, keep flame away from what it can ignite and from the plastic components nearby, and carry the weight of a full vessel on the floor or a stand rather than on the piping.

included: identifying found materials and their accepted transitions
dielectric separation of dissimilar metals
method trade-offs across joining techniques
torque and sealant discipline on plastic components
potable-listed materials
support of vessel weight
hot-work precautions
excluded: whole-house repiping
asserting a specific product listing as universally required
the leak-test procedure itself

pros.claim: Matching the connection method to the material actually found keeps every joint inside the conditions it was designed for
pros.example: using a dielectric transition where the new assembly meets old galvanized pipe instead of screwing dissimilar metals together

cons.claim: The most reliable and serviceable method is often the slowest per joint or the most expensive to tool up for
cons.example: a press system that pays for itself in reliability but ties up capital before the volume justifies it

failure_modes: over-torquing a plastic bypass or valve thread so it cracks days later
joining dissimilar metals with no dielectric transition and seeding corrosion at the newest joint
disturbing brittle galvanized pipe without warning the customer that it may cascade
acceptance_tests: every joint uses a transition accepted for the two materials it joins, plastic connections follow the manufacturer's sealant and torque instructions, and vessel weight is carried by the floor or a stand rather than by the piping
revisit_triggers: one joint type starts appearing in callbacks
a manufacturer revises its fitting or sealant instructions
a pipe material not previously seen appears in the service area

base.update_signal: callback analysis links failures to a specific joining method or fitting batch

nodes.definition: Treat water damage as the defining catastrophic risk of this trade and engineer against it deliberately, because one soaked finished floor can consume the margin of many installs and travels straight into reviews, insurance history and the owner's reputation. The controls are layered rather than singular: pressurize the finished assembly and hold it while every joint is inspected under pressure instead of glanced at while wet; run a full regeneration or backwash cycle so the joints see the dynamic pressure swings and the drain sees the real flow; site and pan the equipment so an eventual failure drains rather than soaks; offer a leak sensor or automatic shutoff as a named option with its limits stated honestly wherever the exposure is high, such as above a finished space; confirm the homeowner can actually operate the bypass; and set an explicit follow-up rule for the first days, when a slow weep declares itself. The photographic record of each joint under pressure and the recorded test result is what makes any later dispute resolvable instead of a matter of two recollections.

included: pressure hold and inspection under pressure
a full dynamic cycle run with the crew present
pan and drain-aware siting
leak sensor or automatic shutoff offered with honest limits
homeowner bypass competence
first-days follow-up rule
photographic joint record
excluded: insurance advice or any statement about what a policy will cover
remediation of pre-existing water damage
service-plan design

pros.claim: A held pressure test plus a full cycle catches the weeping joint while the crew is still standing in the room
pros.example: a fitting that looks dry to a glance and weeps only once regeneration swings the pressure around

cons.claim: Testing and cycling add site time, and the leak-protection option adds cost that many customers decline
cons.example: an extra hour on a job the crew could otherwise have called finished at the last connection

failure_modes: leaving without pressurizing and inspecting the assembly under pressure
installing above a finished space with no pan and no drain path
presenting an automatic shutoff as a guarantee rather than a mitigation with limits
acceptance_tests: the assembly holds pressure for the standard's stated period with no observed weep, a full regeneration or backwash cycle runs with the crew present, and joint photographs plus the recorded test result are stored with the job
revisit_triggers: any leak callback, however small
a change of fitting type, supplier or joining method
a new install location class such as an attic, an upstairs closet or above a finished ceiling

base.update_signal: a leak callback occurs on a job whose pressure test and cycle were recorded as passing

nodes.definition: Turn a physically finished install into a system proven to do what was sold. Commissioning follows a fixed sequence: fill and purge the media so fines and manufacturing residue go to the drain rather than into the customer's aerators; sanitize where the manufacturer or good practice calls for it; program the control valve with the verified hardness and the household's real demand pattern rather than a factory default; set regeneration or backwash to an hour the household does not use water; run a manual cycle from beginning to end while watching the drain and the discharge rate; check flow and pressure at a fixture against the pressure budget; and then take a post-install sample at a treated tap and compare it with the pre-install reading on the same parameters, taken the same way. That matched comparison is the honest proof of performance: it demonstrates the change in the parameters the system was sold to change and nothing else, with no statement about health outcomes, no inference about parameters that were never measured, and no substitution of a demonstration trick for a reading.

included: purge and sanitize
valve programming from verified inputs
regeneration timing set to the household pattern
a full manual cycle observed
flow and pressure check against the budget
matched pre and post treated-tap comparison on the sold parameters
excluded: any health or medical claim drawn from the result
retest cadence used as a retention instrument
diagnostic testing aimed at a new sale

pros.claim: A matched before-and-after on exactly the parameters that were sold gives the customer verifiable proof and gives the business a defensible record
pros.example: a hardness reading at the kitchen tap after the first cycle set beside the same measurement taken before the install

cons.claim: Commissioning adds site time and can expose a shortfall the crew must resolve before it can leave
cons.example: a post-install reading revealing that the valve was left on a default rather than the verified value

failure_modes: leaving the control valve on factory defaults so regeneration never matches the household
skipping the purge so the customer's aerators and fixtures fill with fines
describing a treated-tap improvement as a health benefit rather than a parameter change
acceptance_tests: the commissioning record shows purge and sanitize completed, the programmed settings with the verified inputs they came from, an observed full cycle, a flow and pressure check, and a matched pre and post reading limited to the parameters the system was sold to change
revisit_triggers: the post-install reading does not show the expected change
the customer reports the system is not performing as demonstrated
the manufacturer revises its startup or programming procedure

base.update_signal: post-install readings systematically fail to show the change the sizing model predicted

nodes.definition: Spend the last part of the visit making the homeowner competent and correctly expectant, because most first-year contacts are questions rather than faults. The walkthrough covers where the bypass is and how to work it, what to do first if they see water, which consumable each stage takes and roughly how often this household's load will call for it as a mechanism rather than a promise, what the water will now do differently including the changed feel after softening, the different taste, the spotting that stops or starts, and what the system does not do, stated plainly and including any parameter it was never designed to address plus the explicit statement that no claim is being made about anyone's health. It closes with who to call, what the warranty covers and what it does not, and the written record handed over. It is also the moment where a customer who is elderly, alone, unwell or visibly overwhelmed is offered a second pass, a family member on the phone, or a return visit, rather than a signature collected at the end of a rushed explanation.

included: bypass demonstration and emergency instruction
consumable expectations explained as a load mechanism
sensory and performance changes to expect
an explicit statement of what the system does not do
warranty scope and contact routing
vulnerable-customer pacing at handoff
excluded: selling the service plan or quoting its price
health guidance of any kind
renegotiating scope or price at the door

pros.claim: A homeowner who can bypass the system and knows what to expect generates fewer emergency calls and fewer disappointed reviews
pros.example: a customer who turns the bypass and calls the office in the morning instead of an emergency plumber overnight

cons.claim: A thorough orientation lengthens an already long visit and some customers simply want the crew gone
cons.example: a handoff compressed into two minutes because the customer has to leave, so the bypass is never actually demonstrated

failure_modes: leaving without the customer having physically operated the bypass
overstating what the system removes or letting the customer infer a health benefit
letting a rushed handoff stand in for understanding with a customer who is clearly not following
acceptance_tests: the handoff record confirms the customer operated the bypass, the consumable expectation and its basis were explained, the statement of what the system does not do was made, and warranty scope and contact routing were left in writing
revisit_triggers: a support call asks something the orientation was supposed to cover
a review or complaint describes a surprise after installation
the orientation content or the equipment class changes

base.update_signal: first-year support calls cluster on a topic the orientation already claims to cover

nodes.definition: Close the job with the record everything afterwards depends on. The as-built captures what was installed with model and serial numbers, the configuration and stage order, the programmed settings together with the verified inputs behind them, the placement and the joint photographs taken under pressure, the waste connection arrangement, every locally verified compliance item with the authority consulted and the date, every change order with its approval, and the pre and post readings. It also fixes the warranty picture honestly, because manufacturer coverage typically depends on conditions the installation must satisfy, such as installing to the manufacturer's instructions, operating inside stated water-quality and pressure limits, and sometimes registration and documented maintenance, while workmanship is the installer's own promise with its own stated period; the boundary between the two is written down at handoff rather than discovered during a dispute. The finished record is the artifact the recurring service relationship stands on: without it the next technician is guessing and the service plan is priced blind.

included: as-built configuration, serials and programmed settings
joint and placement photographs
dated compliance verifications
approved change orders
pre and post readings
manufacturer condition-based coverage separated from the workmanship promise
handoff of the record to the service function
excluded: service-plan tiers, cadence and pricing
legal interpretation of warranty terms
insurance advice

pros.claim: A complete as-built converts every future service visit from an investigation into a scheduled task
pros.example: a technician arriving two years later already knowing the stage order and the exact cartridges without opening anything

cons.claim: Assembling the record properly costs crew time at the end of a long day, exactly when the temptation to file it later is strongest
cons.example: photographs that never get uploaded and a settings sheet reconstructed from memory a month afterwards

failure_modes: recording the model but not the serial or the programmed settings
promising coverage the manufacturer's conditions do not actually support
leaving compliance verifications undocumented so nobody can later show what was checked
acceptance_tests: the job cannot be closed until the record holds the configuration, serials, programmed settings, joint and placement photographs, dated compliance verifications, approved change orders and the pre and post readings, with manufacturer conditions and workmanship terms stated separately
revisit_triggers: a warranty claim is refused on a condition the record cannot evidence
a service visit finds the as-built does not match what is on the wall
the manufacturer changes its warranty conditions or registration requirements

base.update_signal: a warranty denial or a service visit exposes a gap the as-built record should have closed

edges.why_related: the fixture inventory and simultaneous-use picture that the demand profile rests on are gathered during the physical walk of the house
placement can only be fixed once the tie-in, shutoff, heater position, drain, receptacle, clearance and carry path have been observed
the grain load and the iron compensation that size the softener come directly from the verified chemistry parameters
media class and bed life follow from the disinfectant class and the concentration being reduced
the oxidizable load and the sediment picture decide which pretreatment stages a well design must carry
daily volume converts hardness into a daily grain load and peak flow sets the vessel and valve that must pass it
the budget is evaluated at the profile's peak simultaneous flow rather than at an average draw
who may lawfully perform the connection is one of the obligation classes verified before the labor model is chosen
the acceptable waste connection and the permitted discharge destination are locally verified obligations, not design preferences
the required cross-connection protection class and the treatment of a closed system are set by the authority having jurisdiction
receptacle protection requirements and bonding continuity restoration are obligation classes verified locally before the equipment is energized
the sequence can only be drawn once the softener's vessel, backwash behaviour and protection needs are known
which stage must shield the carbon bed and where the sacrificial cartridge belongs follow from the media choice
the physical footprint and the order of the stages determine how much wall and floor the loop must occupy and in what direction it runs
the bypass, isolation valves and drain-down are cut into the loop that placement defines
the joints that leak control tests and photographs are the joints the material and method decision produced
a system is not commissioned until it has held pressure and run a full cycle without weeping
the orientation explains a system that has already been programmed, cycled and verified, and uses the verified reading as its honest proof
the programmed settings, observed cycle and matched readings are the substance of the as-built record
